item.title: Nordic Data Center Group ASP Is Said to Weigh Oslo Stock Listing
item.description: AI infrastructure developer ASP Data Center AS is considering an initial public offering in Oslo that could raise the equivalent of about $100 million, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Mayo Cerqueiro and Natasha Voase

item.title: Paramount Completes Acquisition of Warner Bros.
item.description: Paramount Skydance closed its $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery on Tuesday, completing one of the biggest media mergers of all time. Hannah Miller reports on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Uber to Buy EzCater for $2.3 Billion in Enterprise Push
item.description: Uber Technologies Inc. is buying catering firm ezCater Inc. for $2.3 billion in a cash deal that will help the Uber Eats delivery platform reach a more corporate clientele.
item.dc:creator: Natalie Lung

item.title: AI to See Massive Adoption 'Unseen' in Previous Tech Cycles, Says Neostellar Principal
item.description: American AI companies’ performance lead over China narrowed sharply in past months to a record low after labs such as DeepSeek gained ground, threatening US tech supremacy, according to Bloomberg Intelligence. Willy Lee, Principal at Neostellar, offers his view from the VC world when it comes to AI investments and the IPO market. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia Heads for $6 Trillion Value as Chips Rally
item.description: Nvidia is nearing a $6 trillion market capitalization as investors return to the AI chipmaker after a disappointing start to the year. Carmen Reinicke reports on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: JPMorgan's Dimon Weighs In on AI Boom, Bond Selloff and UK Banks
item.description: JPMorgan Chase Chairman and CEO Jamie Dimon discusses the issues behind financing the AI boom, the global bond selloff and the state of UK banks. He speaks with Tom Mackenzie at JPMorgan's Tech Stars Conference in London. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Google Accused of Overcharging 20 Million Consumers in UK Class Action
item.description: Google was accused of overcharging Android app developers for over a decade, leading to inflated prices on the Play Store for about 20 million UK customers.
item.dc:creator: Jeremy Hodges and Samuel Stolton

item.title: ASML’s Chip Technology Move Threatens Besi Shares, BofA Says
item.description: BE Semiconductor Industries NV’s share price doesn’t reflect the threat from fellow Dutch company ASML Holding NV in terms of an advanced chip packaging technique, Bank of America analysts said.
item.dc:creator: Henry Ren

item.title: Nvidia Soars Near $6 Trillion Market Cap With Stock Back at High
item.description: Nvidia Corp. is on the verge of becoming the first company with a $6 trillion market capitalization as investors rotate back into the artificial-intelligence chipmaker after a disappointing start to the year.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Vlastelica and Carmen Reinicke

item.title: Mythos Drove Up Cyber Risk 10-Fold, Says JPMorgan's Dimon
item.description: JPMorgan Chase & Co. Chief Executive Officer Jamie Dimon says artificial intelligence has exposed new vulnerabilities for banks. He says the risks of cyber attacks have gone up 10-fold since the release of Anthropic's Mythos ai model. He speaks exclusively to Bloomberg's Tom Mackenzie at the JPMorgan Tech Stars Conference in London. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Singapore’s DayOne Files for US IPO Joining Data Center Rush
item.description: DayOne Data Centers Ltd. filed for a US initial public offering, setting the Singapore-headquartered firm up to capture investors’ resilient demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure.
item.dc:creator: Anthony Hughes

item.title: Wayve CEO Kendall on the Future of Driving
item.description: Wayve CEO Alex Kendall discusses the future of driving, the market for autonomous vehicles in the US and China, as well as the possibility of a future IPO. He spoke with Bloomberg TV's Tom Mackenzie on the sidelines of the JPMorgan Tech Stars conference in London. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: OpenAI and Anthropic Face Rising Price Pressure From Big AI Users
item.description: AI-powered software startups are increasingly turning to cheaper open models
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Torrence

item.title: UAE's Al Bannai on AI Developments
item.description: Faisal Al Bannai, adviser to the President of the United Arab Emirates, speaks with Bloomberg's Alex Dooler at the 'AI Everything' conference in Abu Dhabi. He talks about the launch of a new model of Falcon AI that's more attuned to the Emirati dialect, as well as saying he sees some exciting start-ups in the fields of robotics, driving and security. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Seagate, Toshiba Said to Vie for TDK’s Hard-Drive Head Unit
item.description: Seagate Technology Holdings Plc and Toshiba Corp. are locked in a contest for TDK Corp.’s magnetic-heads business for hard-disk drives, as the two rivals try to keep pace with demand for AI data-center storage devices.
item.dc:creator: Kentaro Tsutsumi and Takashi Mochizuki

item.title: AI Subscription Models Tested as Few Consumers Pay
item.description: Subscription models may not be enough of a lure.
item.dc:creator: Natalie Lung

item.title: OpenAI in $30 Billion Round Talks With BlackRock, UAE Funds
item.description: OpenAI is in talks with multiple investment funds from the United Arab Emirates to help anchor a $30 billion round of financing, according to people familiar with the matter. BlackRock is also in discussions to participate in the round. Ruhell Amin reports on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: JPMorgan Tops Global AI Banking Index for Fifth Straight Year
item.description: JPMorgan Chase & Co. held its spot as the world’s most advanced bank in artificial intelligence for a fifth straight year, widening its lead over rivals in an annual ranking that shows AI deployment across the industry is accelerating at a record pace.
item.dc:creator: Rthvika Suvarna

item.title: MNT-Halan Plans $150 Million IPO, Egypt’s Biggest Since 2021
item.description: Egyptian fintech unicorn MNT-Halan is seeking to raise 7.84 billion pounds ($150 million), in what would be the country’s biggest initial public offering in dollar terms for about five years.
item.dc:creator: Tarek El-Tablawy

item.title: AMD Chief Sees Very High Demand, Urges AI Firms to Cooperate
item.description: Advanced Micro Devices Inc.’s Lisa Su predicted “very high” chip demand continuing for the next few years, even as the industry faces challenges such as concerns over AI’s safety.
item.dc:creator: Debby Wu
